obtained.how: not obtained: an unpublished 1982 MSc thesis (University of Toronto), not in U of T's repository. Read only as relayed by Chu 2001 (PhD thesis, University of Toronto; already fetched for its own entry)

bibliography.checked_against: Chu 2001's reference list (PDF p. 124) only; the thesis's title page not seen
bibliography.note: Chu 2001 lists it exactly as cited: Post, E.E. 1982. Some factors influencing the reproductive effort of smallmouth bass in two Ontario lakes. M.Sc. Thesis, University of Toronto, Toronto, Ontario.

claims.claim: only 12–47 % of mature males spawned in a given year (Lake Opeongo; Post 1982, via Chu 2001)
claims.note: Thesis not read. The relay is faithful: Chu 2001, PDF p. 16, 'The percentage of the mature male population spawning in Lake Opeongo, Ontario in any given year was estimated to be between 12 and 47% (Post 1982)'. Chu gives no years, n or method. Chu also relays (PDF p. 112) that in Opeongo 'only fish 4 and older nest (Post 1982' and a personal communication).

tried.note: University of Toronto repository (TSpace): no record of the thesis (84 hits, none by Post; a phrase search of the title gave 0)
no DOI or URL exists; a 1982 U of T MSc thesis may survive only in print or on Theses Canada microfiche (Library and Archives Canada), not searched online here

notes: Keep the citation as 'Post 1982, via Chu 2001' (as the paper does), or cite Chu 2001 for it. A checked figure of the same kind exists: Raffetto, Baylis & Serns 1990 (Nebish Lake, Wisconsin, read in full in this batch) found 11, 33, 31 and 31 % of the estimated mature males bred in 1982–85 (their Table 2, p. 1528). It could stand beside or replace the Opeongo range.
